title: What is User Input?
overview: User input allows users to enter and provide data inside a React Native application. It is commonly used in forms such as login, registration, search, and profile screens.

example.title: User Input Example
example.content:
Common user inputs:
• Name
• Email
• Password
• Search Text
• Feedback

title: TextInput Component
overview: TextInput is a core React Native component used to accept text input from users. It provides various properties to control input behavior, appearance, and validation.

example.title: Basic TextInput Example
example.content:
import { TextInput } from 'react-native';

<TextInput
 placeholder="Enter your name"
/>

title: Managing Input Value with State
overview: The value entered by users is stored using state. The useState hook keeps track of the input value and updates the UI whenever the user types something.

title: TextInput Important Props
overview: TextInput provides many properties to customize user input behavior, keyboard type, security, and user experience.

example.title: Common TextInput Props
example.content:
placeholder
value
onChangeText
keyboardType
secureTextEntry
maxLength
autoCapitalize

title: Handling Forms in React Native
overview: Forms combine multiple input fields to collect user information. React Native uses state and event handlers to manage form values and submit data.

example.title: Form Example
example.content:
Login Form:
• Email Input
• Password Input
• Submit Button
• Validation

title: Input Validation
overview: Input validation checks whether the entered data is correct before processing it. It helps prevent invalid data submission and improves user experience.

example.title: Validation Example
example.content:
Email should contain @
Password should have minimum characters
Required fields should not be empty

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned how to handle user input using TextInput, manage values with state, use important TextInput properties, create forms, and validate user-entered data.
